title: Comparison view — next steps
summary: Revision 2, after Zach answered the open questions: visual/appearance diff is IN (driver: golden layouts) as a second profile of one engine; merge AND rebase return as N7; the chrome ports into the editor kit; ‘one paint, two producers’ honoured through two props; and the id-association research is digested with citations — the prior work already answered it. Three lanes (N1, N7, N8) are dispatchable today. Lane-readable spec: docs/COMPARISON-NEXT-STEPS.md.
changes: N1 — propertyRows over SceneDiff (S–M, unblocked): donor propertyRows.ts:216,243 re-expressed over our diff rows. Write set: src/scene/propertyRows.ts + test + story.

N7 — merge + rebase math (M, unblocked, Q3 “we want to support both”): applySceneDiff + diff3Scene(base, a, b) → {merged, conflicts}; rebase = replay onto b through the same apply. Conflicts reported, never auto-resolved. Write set: src/scene/merge.ts + test + story.

N8 — appearance diff (S–M, unblocked for revision pairs, Q1's golden-layouts driver): a second profile of diffScene — matched pairs compared on geometry (classifyPoseChange, shipped) + appearance props, per-element, threshold-free. Write set: src/scene/appearanceDiff.ts + test + story.

N2 — diff paint on the components (M–L, barrier: components + skin lanes): per-component diff?: DiffMark, DIFF_VARIANT_TRAITS verbatim as data, channel discipline + corner rule, changed-AND-broken proven with measured geometry. Still the one that matters.
N3 — six-variant gallery (S, after N2). S5 — useLinkedCameras + blend (S, barrier: hosts lane) — now the enabling mechanism behind Q4's chosen Figma overlay slider, not one option among views.

S6 — PropertyTable (M, needs N1 + components lane) and N6 — CompareBar · DiffCodeView · CompareView story (M, needs N2+S5+S6): editor-kit components with their own stories per Q3 — the dialog's modal shell stays app wiring.

N9 — conformance identity ladder over BlockScene (M, triggered by golden testing, not by a lane): the pyblocks ladder pre-scoped as a port map (name→definitionId, graph→producersOf/consumersOf, source→a portsOf-style resolver, unmatched first-class).
S7 — still deferred; un-defer conditions unchanged, port-rename detection now slightly likelier once golden testing surfaces renamed ports.
New stories carry the tags convention: tags: ["area:blocks", "lane:<slug>"].
findings: Q2 reconciled in Zach's favour: “one paint, two producers” is exactly what gets built — one visual language, one channel discipline, shared severity tokens, two producers marking the same element — delivered through two props, because his own aside (“some specific diff paint we will need”) names the reason: token ink, pose ghosts and chips have no home in a Diagnostic, and added/removed/modified has no rank for max(severity). Merge rule for changed-AND-broken unchanged.

Q1 verdict: both diffs ship as two profiles of one engine, not two engines — the shape pyblocks measured its way to. The raw file/token diff survives as the cheap boolean oracle (an id-free drawable-props fingerprint: 30 canonicalizations, 0 drift), not as the engine — a raw record diff on a passing case reported 40+ changes with zero meaning. Pixel render-compare stays deliberately outside the differ: detects but cannot explain, re-imports thresholds; returns only if rendering itself becomes the subject.

Q3 confirms the CRDT tripwire rather than disturbing it: diff3Scene takes the merge base as an ordinary scene argument — a pair of documents, never a field on one — so merge and rebase land with BlockScene still {nodes, edges}. CVP §4 predicted exactly this.

The id-association research already answered Zach's question. His two cases are the two shipped profiles of pyblocks/board_diff.py:80-90: mutated file = revision (id rung only, layout is signal), generated copy = conformance (id→name→graph→source→unmatched, layout ignored). The similarity rung was a deliberate deletion — the probe had a 0.45 floor, shipped identity.py removed it, a test asserts its absence against the parsed AST, and 450/450 blocks still resolve (355 name · 51 graph · 44 source · 0 unmatched). Open work recorded: the designed-but-unimplemented write-back migration. Map note: zach_brain/Projects/bbox-ui/MOC - Visual Diff.md.

Read properly this time: the pyblocks probes and work orders in full, the engine report and architecture report as stripped text, the shipped identity.py/board_diff.py headers — both prior lanes had only listed these. The multi-MB visual-vocabulary pages remain unopened; their conclusions enter through DIFF_VARIANT_TRAITS (code) and the MOC's digest of the round-2 correction.

Baselines re-verified after the tags merge: unit 24 files / 393, stories 46 files / 188 (the −4 is exactly the retired WhatsNew stories), tsc clean. Donor citations from revision 1 all still hold; §6's new pyblocks citations verified against the tree today.
